hints: Look at the position and texture of each label. P is the thick outer boundary, Q is the large pale empty-looking space, and R shows stacked membranes.
Remember how to tell a chloroplast from a mitochondrion in EM (grana stacks vs small sausage shape), and how to tell the nucleolus (small dark dot) from the whole nucleus.
walkthrough:
**Start with P, the outer edge**

Look at the far left edge of the cell. You can see a thick, dark, rigid layer shared with the neighbour cell. That is classic plant cell wall, not the thin cell surface membrane. So P = cell wall. This already rules out A and B.

**Identify Q and R by size and internal detail**

Q is the very large, pale, almost empty region taking up much of the cell. That is the plant vacuole filled with cell sap. R is the large organelle full of parallel membranes with dark stacked discs. Those stacks are grana made of thylakoids, so R = chloroplast, not a small mitochondrion.

**Zoom in on S inside the nucleus**

The large grainy area at the bottom is the nucleus, but label S points only to the small, very dense dark dot inside it. That dense region where ribosomal RNA is made is the nucleolus. So S = nucleolus, not the whole nucleus.

Putting it together: P = cell wall, Q = vacuole, R = chloroplast, S = nucleolus.

options.A: Incorrect. P is the thick cell wall, not membrane, Q is the vacuole, R is a chloroplast with grana, and S is only the nucleolus.
options.B: Gets Q and R right but wrong on P and S. P is the cell wall and S is the nucleolus inside the nucleus, not the whole nucleus.
options.C: Gets P and S right but swaps Q and R. Q is the large vacuole, not cytoplasm, and R is a chloroplast with thylakoid stacks, not a mitochondrion.
options.D: Correct. P is cell wall, Q is vacuole, R is chloroplast with grana, and S is the dense nucleolus within the nucleus.
